lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me. I'm asking about one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start with some basic questions:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, I need to understand his current situation as the eligibility rules are specific for children aged 16-19.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure to be honest. He's doing something at college, but I don't know if that counts as "approved" or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay - I can help clarify. College courses often do count as approved education. Let me ask a few questions to help determine this:

**What type of course is Alex doing at college? For example, is it a full-time course like A-levels, a BTEC, a vocational qualification, or something else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm really not sure what type of course it is. He just started at college but I don't know the details about what qualification he's working towards or whether it's full-time or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's quite common for parents not to have all the details. Let me ask about your own circumstances now, which are also important for eligibility.

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you, that's helpful. Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's situation regarding work and benefits:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, is it for 24 hours or more per week? Also, is he receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all. And no, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask about whether anyone else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else (such as another parent or family member) claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him, and no one else is claiming it either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now, let me ask about your immigration and residency status, as this can affect eligibility:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another immigration status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now let me go back to Alex's education situation, as this is the key factor for his eligibility at age 17.

You mentioned he's doing something at college but you're not sure of the details. Let me ask this:

**Do you know if Alex is attending college on most weekdays, or does he just go in occasionally? And has he registered with a careers service or is he planning to join the armed services?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He goes in most weekdays as far as I know. And no, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that - he's not planning to join the armed forces either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful - the fact that he's attending college most weekdays suggests it's likely a full-time course.

Let me ask one more question to help determine eligibility:

**Do you know approximately when Alex started this college course? Was it recently (like September), or has he been going for a while? And do you know if the course is expected to continue, or has he mentioned leaving or finishing soon?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't really know when exactly he started or how long the course is supposed to last. Sorry, I just don't have those details.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - I understand you don't have all the specific details about Alex's course.

Let me assess your situation based on what you've told me:

**Summary of your situation:**
- Alex is 17 years old
- He lives with you in the UK (Manchester)
- You are a British citizen
- Alex is not working and doesn't receive any benefits in his own right
- Alex is attending college most weekdays
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**The key issue:** For a 17-year-old to be eligible for Child Benefit, they must be in "approved education or training." This typically includes full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels, BTECs, NVQs up to level 3, etc.) of at least 12 hours per week of supervised study.

Since Alex is attending college most weekdays, this strongly suggests he may be in approved education. However, you've told me you don't know:
- The type of course or qualification he's studying for
- Whether it's officially full-time
- When he started or how long it will last

**Without these details, I cannot definitively determine whether Alex's college course meets the criteria for "approved education."** To successfully claim Child Benefit, you would need to be able to confirm these details to HMRC when you apply.

- The type of course (A-levels, BTEC, NVQ, etc.)
- Whether it's full-time (at least 12 hours supervised study per week)

If you want to apply for Child Benefit, I'd recommend finding out these details about Alex's course from him or his college. You'll likely need this information when making your claim to HMRC anyway. If the course is full-time non-advanced education, you would likely be eligible to claim.
